scenario: A rare-disease clinical research team prepares a peer-reviewed paper supplementary data table describing a small pediatric cohort. The agent pipeline: (1) pseudonymize the raw patient-level records removing HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers (names, DOBs, NHS/MRN numbers, postcodes/ZIP codes, phone numbers); (2) clean and standardize the de-identified data into SDTM-compliant demographics and lab tables, normalizing dates and filling missing values; (3) generate the final publication package — a cohort description table and methods narrative — suitable for journal submission as supplementary data.
info_flow: redacta pseudonymizes the raw patient records (removes names, DOBs, postcodes, MRN numbers) → clinical-data-cleaner standardizes the cleaned data into SDTM DM domain fields (AGE, RFSTDTC, SITEID, RACE, SEX) and computes a per-patient row → reporting assembles a publication-ready supplementary cohort table and methods section from the standardized rows.
